strengths: Strong empirical results with substantial improvements over state-of-the-art in-context learning (GVL), achieving 3x better VOC in many cases
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple distribution shifts (environment, embodiment, task) with systematic dataset design
Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations of existing approaches for progress estimation in robotic manipulation
Clear methodology combining meta-learning with test-time adaptation and thoughtful dissimilarity-based sampling to encourage semantic understanding
Thorough ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating the value of implicit memory over trajectory-level or reset-based adaptation
Good reproducibility with detailed architectural specs, hyperparameters, and training procedures in appendices
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty - primarily applies existing techniques (Sun et al. 2020 test-time training, Finn et al. 2017 meta-learning) to a new domain without significant innovation

Insufficient explanation of the critical self-supervised loss component: projection matrices P_V, P_K, P_Q introduced with minimal justification; learning procedure and reconstruction objective structure not clearly specified

Narrow experimental scope: training limited to 2,986 demonstrations from single robot in ToyKitchen; all evaluations remain within similar robotic manipulation settings; claims of 'generalizable task progress estimation' overstated

Unfair baseline comparison: GVL not designed for progress estimation; no ablation showing impact of fine-tuning GVL on this task; critical missing computational cost analysis comparing test-time adaptation overhead vs. GVL inference

Scalability concerns unaddressed: method requires full trajectory access at inference time; applicability to online/streaming settings unclear; computational complexity with trajectory length not analyzed

Incomplete analysis: no error analysis or discussion of failure cases (e.g., ms_sweep VOC of 0.4898 vs. 0.6-0.8 for others); no visualization of learned representations; missing sensitivity analysis on hyperparameters like window size k

Technical clarity issues: meta-learning procedure underspecified (gradient backpropagation through adaptation steps?); fundamental tension between assuming monotonic progress (t/T) and stated goal of mitigating temporal bias
Evaluation limitations: VOC metric measures chronological order alignment but may not suit all tasks; no justification for metric choice or exploration of alternatives
